prerequisites: Ability to construct mathematical reasoning and prove theorems
Basic knowledge of programming as taught in Methodology of Computer Science or Computer Science in secondary education

learning_outcomes.text: The student has knowledge of the basic principles of propositional logic and various proof schemes.
The student knows discrete mathematical structures such as graphs, trees, and state machines, can recognize their most important properties, and knows how they are used to model engineering problems.
The student can recognize mathematical algorithms related to discrete mathematical structures and assess their advantages and disadvantages.
The student is familiar with applications of discrete mathematics, as well as the place discrete mathematics occupies in engineering thinking.

syllabus_topics: Recurrence relations & associated analysis regarding divide-and-conquer algorithms
Definitions and elementary principles of Graph algorithms
Euler and Hamiltonian paths in graphs
Some applications and examples of Graph algorithms
Some applications and examples of State machines
Principles of AI using the above
Neural networks (connecting to graphs and as a computational framework)
State machines to model various problems

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period

bibliography: Course notes and slides from the lecturers
